name: download_version
title: Download a specified version of a CRAN package

origin.description: It downloads the package to a temporary file, and returns the name of the file.
origin.usage: download_version(package, version = NULL, repos = getOption("repos"), type = getOption("pkgType"), ...)

arguments.name: package
arguments.text: Name of the package to install.

arguments.name: version
arguments.text: Version of the package to install. Can either be a string giving the exact version required, or a specification in the same format as the parenthesized expressions used in package dependencies. One of the following formats: an exact version required, as a string, e.g. "0.1.13"; a comparison operator and a version, e.g. ">= 0.1.12"; several criteria to satisfy, as a comma-separated string, e.g. ">= 1.12.0, < 1.14"; several criteria to satisfy, as elements of a character vector, e.g. c(">= 1.12.0", "< 1.14").

arguments.name: repos
arguments.text: Character vector, the base URL(s) of the repositories to use, e.g., the URL of a CRAN mirror such as "https://cloud.r-project.org".

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: Character, indicating the type of package to download and install. Will be "source" except on Windows and some macOS builds.
Other arguments passed on to utils::install.packages(). download_version accepts them and does not use them.

origin.details: A missing version selects the current row from available.packages on contrib.url. A version such as "2.5.0" is treated as ==. The repositories are checked in order, current rows first, then each archive. An older tarball is the last matching row of src/contrib/Meta/archive.rds, whose row names are package/package_version.tar.gz. The file is written to tempfile().
origin.example:
path <- download_version("remotes", "2.5.0", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org", type = "source")
files <- untar(path, list = TRUE)
desc <- files[grepl("DESCRIPTION$", files)][[1]]
ex <- tempfile()
dir.create(ex)
untar(path, files = desc, exdir = ex)
dcf <- read.dcf(file.path(ex, desc))
base <- paste0(dcf[1, "Package"], "_", dcf[1, "Version"], ".tar.gz")
cat(paste0('download_version("remotes", "2.5.0", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org", type = "source") downloads ', base, '.\n'))

translation.description: It downloads the package to a temporary file, and returns the name of the file.

arguments.name: version
arguments.text: Version to download. None selects the current contrib row. "2.5.0" means == 2.5.0. A comparison such as ">= 2.0.0, < 2.4.0", or a list of criteria, uses the same operators as a package dependency.

arguments.name: repos
arguments.text: Base URL of a CRAN-like repository, or a list or dict of them. Default https://cloud.r-project.org.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: Package type passed to the contrib URL. "source" reads src/contrib. "both" and, on Linux, "binary" are source. Default "source".

arguments.name: extra
arguments.text: Further arguments are accepted and ignored.

translation.details: The current row is read from the contrib PACKAGES index, with the R version and OS_type filters. "2.5" and "2.5.0" compare equal. An older version is taken from src/contrib/Meta/archive.rds, gzip around an XDR version-2 file. The tarball names are that data frame's row names, and the last row that satisfies the version is used. The download uses urllib and follows redirects. The returned path is a temporary file; its basename is not the tarball name.
translation.example:
from remotes.download_version import download_version
import tarfile
path = download_version("remotes", "2.5.0", repos="https://cloud.r-project.org", type="source")
with tarfile.open(path, "r:gz") as tar:
    name = next(n for n in tar.getnames() if n.endswith("DESCRIPTION"))
    text = tar.extractfile(name).read().decode()
fields = {}
for line in text.splitlines():
    if ":" in line and not line[:1].isspace():
        key, value = line.split(":", 1)
        fields[key] = value.strip()
base = fields["Package"] + "_" + fields["Version"] + ".tar.gz"
print('download_version("remotes", "2.5.0", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org", type = "source") downloads ' + base + '.')
